explicit_user_authorization.scope: Repair the optimizer so it actually optimizes the full existing automation pool instead of leaving roles stopped.
authorizes: reversible schedule staggering of existing managed roles
increasing the existing optimizer task's guard cadence
a canary timing-mode or terminal-method experiment if staggering does not solve persistence
forbids: disabling, pausing, deleting, replacing or reducing the 19-role pool
changing the primary O execution or protected recovery monitor
weakening Phase-1 zero-residual-Work, zero-finite-quota or zero-cost gates

finding.evidence: Control12 recorded the fourth recurrence: 8 of 19 intended roles were physically disabled after invocation and were merely re-enabled. The latest user observation reports the pool stopped again.
finding.root_cause_status: For multi_agent, platform/runtime post-invocation disable after noncompletion is directly evidenced. For other roles, the same recurrent lifecycle pattern remains the leading hypothesis but must be tested per role.
finding.critical_path: Keep 19/19 physically runnable and remove or route around the lifecycle persistence defect before spending full optimizer effort on lower-priority semantic portfolio churn.

selected_method.reason: It preserves all roles and task identities, reduces minute-0 queue concentration, bounds stopped time with guard slots, and provides a falsifiable persistence experiment without quota-bearing infrastructure.
required_sequence: Re-enable every stopped intended enabled_desired role and exact-readback.
Update the same existing optimizer task to the authorized guard/full schedule and read back.
Apply the deterministic staggered schedule map to the same existing role task ids and read back every task.
Persist before/after schedule, enabled, last_run and updated_at evidence.
Continue full Phase-1 role-and-method optimization after physical reconciliation.
selected_method.do_not: Do not write another temporary 19/19 snapshot and wait for the next recurrence. Re-enable-only remains emergency repair, not the claimed solution.

acceptance.minimum_survival: Every intended role stays enabled through two consecutive invocation boundaries with later live readback.

fallback_and_switching.if_staggering_fails: Capture exact current-control terminal receipt and platform boundary, immediately re-enable the same task, then test one non-primary canary with condition_watch or a repository-defined noncompletion terminal method. Preserve all roles and schedules not under canary test.
fallback_and_switching.comparison: Use successful-slot coverage, enabled survival, useful output, conflict/duplicate rate, optimizer overhead and expected time-to-root.
fallback_and_switching.rollback: Restore preserved prior schedules only if matched evidence shows the new map is worse; never disable roles or lower the denominator.

history_preservation.control12: Retained in Git history as the fourth-drift evidence and multi_agent platform-lifecycle proof.
history_preservation.physical_state12: Retained as the last exact 19/19 readback before the user's new stop observation.

exact_next_action: The optimizer must apply SCHEDULER_OPTIMIZATION revision1 on its next execution: live-read, re-enable stopped roles, change its own cadence, stagger the same 18 worker/support role task schedules, exact-readback all 19 plus the protected monitor, persist an application receipt, then continue role-and-method optimization.
